newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal rejects notion of zero coupon bonds - IGCP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal rejects notion of zero coupon bonds - IGCP.

text.p: Issuing zero coupon bonds as a way of reducing debt financing cost in any particular year, recently given the green light by Eurostat, amounts to bad debt management, Portugal's state debt manager said.

"Taking financing decisions simply to gain artificial and cosmetic advantages is a bad way to operate," Vitor Bento, chairman of the Institute for Public Credit Management (IGPC), told Reuters in an interview.

Eurostat, the European Union body which overees government accounting practices, announced earlier this month that it was acceptable for the cost of zero coupon debt to be accounted for at expiry. This could help governments save money in any particular year to cut budget deficits.
Bento said that he expected Eurostat to revise its ruling again within three years.

Economic and monetary union (EMU) is due to start at the beginning of 1999 based on economic performance in 1997 and a number of European Union members face problems in meeting budget deficit targets for entry.
